key_insight: The paper shows that combining data storytelling with interpretable machine learning can make AI decisions easier for non-experts to understand without exposing sensitive data or model details.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical explainability layer for AI systems used in high-stakes engineering and public-facing applications where transparency and privacy must both be preserved.
method: Defines data storytelling for interpretable machine learning using the DIST Pyramid
Introduces an I-P-O model and an architecture with separate "What-if" and "Why-not" event generation
Uses data desensitization plus SHAP and LLMs to generate ABT-style narratives
evidence_signal: In the Boston Housing case study, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the "What-if" and "Why-not" stories more comprehensible, with significantly higher accessibility scores than standard SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: The pipeline depends on LLM-generated narratives and desensitization quality, so preserving fidelity while avoiding leakage or misleading simplification is a key implementation risk.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
